svg.title: Why and When to Use Node.js?
svg.desc: Auto-playing 48s step-by-step explainer of "Why and When to Use Node.js?" (from img_4.png). Each step is highlighted in turn with what happens, why it matters, missing concepts added in lime, and a Node.js code example. Hover to pause.
svg.text: Why and When to Use Node.js?
Pros, good use cases, and when to pick something else (or fix it with worker threads)

g.text: Why and When to Use Node.js?
What: Node shines when a server mostly waits on I/O (database, network, files) and struggles
when it must crunch numbers on its single JS thread.
Why: Picking the right tool is a classic interview topic: know both the strengths and the
Added: The "don't use" side has a modern fix (worker_threads), and "preferably NoSQL" is
waiting on I/O? (DB, APIs, files, sockets)
or another language for that service
What: One JS thread with an event loop: while one request waits on the DB, the thread serves
Why: No thread per user means far less memory and context switching under heavy load.
// 3 slow I/O calls in parallel on ONE thread
// total ≈ 120 ms, not 250 ms: the thread never idles
What: Perfect for fast, scalable, data-intensive apps; big companies run it in production.
Why: One language everywhere + npm's huge open-source library = faster, more efficient
What: APIs with a database behind them, data streaming, real-time chat and server-side
Added: "Preferably NoSQL" is outdated: Node works just as well with PostgreSQL/MySQL
(Prisma, pg). Also great for microservices and CLIs.
// thousands of open sockets, one thread
What: Applications with heavy server-side processing (CPU-intensive). Long calculations
block the single JS thread, so every other user waits.
Added: Since Node 12, worker_threads run CPU work on other threads. You can also push jobs
to a queue (BullMQ) or write that one service in another language.
// hash.js: runs on another thread, main stays free
What: Use Node for I/O-heavy, real-time and streaming work. Be careful with CPU-heavy work:
move it off the main thread.
Added: worker_threads, job queues, SQL works fine, microservices / BFF / CLIs as extra use
Image resize per request ~ worker_threads / queue
ML training, video encode ✗ use Python / Go / Rust

svg.text: worker_threads move CPU work off the loop
Heavy loops / sync code in request handlers
Q: When would you NOT choose Node.js?
A: CPU-bound work (or offload it to workers)
